editorial:
You follow Ron Woodroof, a rough-around-the-edges Texas electrician and rodeo guy who gets diagnosed with HIV in 1986 and told he has only 30 days to live. He refuses to accept that fate and starts smuggling unapproved drugs from Mexico and other countries to help himself and others. Along the way he teams up with Rayon, a transgender woman who becomes his unlikely business partner. The vibe is gritty, emotional, and surprisingly funny at times, with a strong 1980s feel.

The acting is the real standout here. Matthew McConaughey lost a ton of weight and gives a raw, powerful performance, and Jared Leto is incredible as Rayon. The pacing keeps you hooked as Ron fights the system and builds his buyers club. The downside is it can feel heavy and sad in places, and some side characters are a bit one-note. If you like true stories about underdogs fighting back, this is for you. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Ron's health has declined badly but he keeps fighting. He wins a legal battle that lets the buyers club keep operating, though the FDA still tries to shut him down. Rayon has already died from AIDS complications. Ron rides his bull one last time at a rodeo, symbolizing he is still alive and fighting. The movie ends with text noting Ron lived seven more years, dying in 1992, far past his 30-day prognosis.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves true stories about underdogs fighting back.
